name: host-data-chart
title: Sparkline from host data
summary: A sparkline drawn from an exported float array the host can replace; the line scales to the array's length, minimum and maximum.
prompt: Draw a sparkline of weekly revenue where the app supplies the numbers as an array of any length.
teaches: Export a float array to the host with resources.floatArrays {"data": {"value": [...], "export": true}}
Derive the series' last index, minimum and range once with canvas variables (arrayLength, arrayMin, arrayMax) and reuse them as @last, @lo, @span
Draw one segment per pair of points with a loop from 0 until @last and arrayGet(@data, i), so a host array of another length or range still fills the chart
Derive the plot area from componentWidth()/componentHeight() so the sparkline stretches to whatever box the host gives it

snippets.note: the exported series and its default
span = max(arrayMax(@data) - @lo, 1): the value range, guarded against a flat series
loop over the points; each segment's ends come from arrayGet

data.meaning: the series to plot, any length >= 2

check.describe: The default series draws a rising teal line ending in a white dot at the top right; render_rc with variables {data: [a falling series]} draws a falling line. Resized, the background fills the box and the sparkline stretches over componentWidth() - 40 by componentHeight() - 80, with the end dot following.

pitfalls: rc-inspect interact doesn't accept float_array variables yet (EXAMPLES_FINDINGS I8); use render_rc variables
Normalising by arrayMax − arrayMin divides by zero when every value is the same; guard the range with max(…, 1)
The loop runs until arrayLength − 1 (one segment per pair), and reads arrayGet(@data, i + 1); looping to arrayLength reads past the end
Plot coordinates written against the header (320 wide, 100 tall) leave the chart stuck at that size; measure the plot area from componentWidth()/componentHeight() instead
